templates.title: Fix a flat tire
templates.prompt: Walk me through fixing a flat bike tire
templates.patches:
{"root":"main","state":{},"elements":{"main":{"type":"Col","props":{"gap":4},"children":["heading","takeaway","steps-title","steps","tools-title","tools-card","safety-title","safety-card"]},"heading":{"type":"Header","props":{"text":"Fix a flat bike tire","size":"2xl"},"children":[]},"takeaway":{"type":"Text","props":{"value":"Remove the wheel, find and patch or replace the tube, then reinstall and check the tire."},"children":[]},"steps-title":{"type":"Header","props":{"text":"Step-by-step","size":"lg"},"children":[]},"steps":{"type":"Steps","props":{"steps":[{"title":"Shift to the smallest rear cog (rear flat) and release the brakes if needed.","detail":"For rim brakes, open the brake’s quick release. For a disc brake, avoid squeezing the brake lever while the wheel is out."},{"title":"Remove the wheel.","detail":"Open the quick-release lever or loosen the axle nuts. For a rear wheel, pull the derailleur back and lift the chain off the smallest cog as the wheel comes free."},{"title":"Deflate and unseat one tire bead.","detail":"If any air remains, press the valve to release it. Use tire levers to lift one bead over the rim; start opposite the valve and work around. Avoid pinching the tube."},{"title":"Take out the tube and locate the puncture.","detail":"Remove the tube, keeping track of how it sat relative to the tire. Inflate it a little and listen or feel for escaping air; water with bubbles can help."},{"title":"Check the tire and rim for the cause.","detail":"Carefully inspect the tire inside and out for glass, thorns, or wire, and remove anything embedded. Check the rim tape and valve hole too. Don’t run a bare finger over sharp debris."},{"title":"Patch or replace the tube.","detail":"For a glue patch, roughen and clean the area, apply vulcanizing fluid, wait until tacky, then press on the patch firmly. Or fit a compatible new tube. Add just enough air to give the tube shape."},{"title":"Refit the tire without pinching the tube.","detail":"Put the valve through the rim, tuck the tube inside, then work the bead back on by hand. Before inflating, inspect both sides to make sure the tube isn’t trapped under the bead."},{"title":"Inflate and reinstall the wheel.","detail":"Inflate to the pressure range printed on the tire sidewall, then reinstall and secure the wheel. Reconnect/opened brakes and confirm the wheel is centered and spins freely."},{"title":"Do a final safety check.","detail":"Squeeze the tire, check that the axle is firmly secured, and test both brakes before riding. If the tire bulges, leaks, or won’t seat evenly, deflate and reseat it."}]},"children":[]},"tools-title":{"type":"Header","props":{"text":"What you’ll need","size":"lg"},"children":[]},"tools-card":{"type":"Card","props":{"title":"Tools & supplies","padding":4},"children":["tools-list"]},"tools-list":{"type":"Markdown","props":{"value":"- Tire levers (2)
- Pump or CO₂ inflator
- Correct-size spare tube **or** patch kit
- Optional: gloves and a small bowl of water for finding a leak"},"children":[]},"safety-title":{"type":"Header","props":{"text":"Important checks","size":"lg"},"children":[]},"safety-card":{"type":"Card","props":{"title":"Before you ride","padding":4},"children":["safety-text"]},"safety-text":{"type":"Text","props":{"value":"Use the pressure range on the tire sidewall—not a generic PSI.
